text:
maya: Hey - opening a docs PR but blocked by a semantics question about Dedicated autoscaling + burst defaults. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/1234

samir: what's the exact ambiguity?

maya: The example in the migration guide shows a Dedicated pool with `autoscale: disabled` and `max_burst: 50` and we had `burst_policy: allow` in the snippet, but runtime previously defaulted to `queue` when unspecified. Need runtime confirmation so docs don't claim the wrong default.

samir: can you paste the snippet you're trying to include?

maya: Sure:
```yaml
dedicated_pools:
  - name: user-facing
    autoscale: disabled
    max_burst: 50
    # burst_policy not set here - what's the runtime default?
```

runtime-eng: short answer: today the dedicated runtime change in v2.3 made the implicit default `burst_policy: queue` for Dedicated pools to protect other tenants on shared infra. Hosted still defaults to `allow` unless quota is hit. but i need to check the rollout tags before we say this in docs (canary -> prod timeline).

ryan: CI preview is failing on the snippet because our docs lint flags unspecified `burst_policy` when `max_burst` present (we treat allow as implicit in linter). docs-bot put a hold: merge-blocker.

docs-bot: @maya Your PR is blocked: linter rule docs/explicit-burst-policy (see https://go/doc-lint/explicit-burst-policy).

maya: ack. If runtime default is indeed `queue` for Dedicated, we can either update the snippet to set `burst_policy: queue` explicitly or change the wording to say "explicitly set `burst_policy` to control behavior". Which is better?

runtime-eng: please add the explicit setting in the snippet to unblock the linter. I'll confirm rollout schedule and post exact version numbers. For the migration guide, saying "explicitly set `burst_policy` in Dedicated configs; runtime defaults to `queue` as of v2.3 in the Dedicated runtime" is safe once I confirm v2.3 is fully rolled.

eva: +1 on explicit setting, and add a short note: "If you rely on impulsive bursts for latency-sensitive paths, consider Hosted API or increase reserved capacity" — helps customers choose.

samir: can we phrase it without committing to a numeric version? some customers read migration docs long after release.

runtime-eng: fair. Suggestion: docs should do both: include explicit snippet (so example is runnable) and include a sentence: "When unspecified, Dedicated pools default to queue semantics. This default may change across runtime versions; set `burst_policy` explicitly to ensure stable behavior." I'll confirm the exact sentence once I check prod roll status.

maya: I'll update the PR with the explicit YAML and that generic sentence. @ryan / @docs-bot can you re-run the linkcheck/lint when I push?

ci-bot: queued re-run for PR 1234 (docs-lint, linkcheck).

ryan: thanks — if runtime-eng confirms before EOD we can merge during the docs merge window, otherwise hold for the next window.

maya: pushed change with explicit `burst_policy: queue` + a parenthetical note about default possibly varying. pinging @runtime-eng to confirm text later.

runtime-eng: saw the push. text looks good, i'll DM a single-line confirmation about v2.3 rollout (should be fully in prod in us-west but not yet in eu). we'll need a small region note if that's relevant.

maya: got it — i'll add a short clause about region rollout only if you confirm it's staggered. for now marking PR as "awaiting runtime confirmation" but lint no longer blocks.

docs-bot: PR 1234 -> label: awaiting-runtime, lint: pass.

maya: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
